clue.text: Dam lake for community leader

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
Superior is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A reservoir lake is being dedicated to a local leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' suggests a reservoir, but here it is the animal-breeding word for a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent, a religious community of nuns, holds this title.

clue.text: Given notice of dismissal, left, right?

definitions.meaning: an order to leave a job or place
the call of left, right is what soldiers on parade march to

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an order to leave, and literally the commands given to troops on parade.

clue.text: Jazz fan in a bed got up for musical performance

indicators.note: in places the jazz fan inside the reversed a-and-bed
got up in a down entry means the words are read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a cot is a small bed
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A jazz lover gets out of bed to play some music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns A COT into TOCA, and CAT goes 'in' it: TOC-CAT-A.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, a showpiece of fast fingerwork.

clue.text: Oriental on top of emaciated tree

indicators.note: on top of in a down entry puts the eastern letter above the thin word

parts.note: E for East, as in the orient
bony means very thin, emaciated

explanation.surface: An Eastern person sits on top of a scrawny tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical tree prized for its very dark hardwood.

clue.text: Whereby she disposes of shells? It's hard to say!

definitions.text: Whereby she disposes of shells? It's hard to say!

parts.words: Whereby she disposes of shells? It's hard to say!
parts.note: recalls the tongue-twister about her selling seashells, the place where she sells them, which is hard to say quickly

explanation.definitionFit: The tongue-twister 'She sells seashells on the ...' ends with this beach word.

clue.text: Verse or essay author's written first

indicators.note: written first says the author is placed before the essay word

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author
an essay is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to write verse or prose, with the author's name heading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a written piece but is the verb meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is writing in metrical lines, so verse in the collective sense.

clue.text: Mars some treasured plane trees

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone damages some cherished plane trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like a verb meaning spoils, but it is the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is nicknamed for its rusty colour as seen from Earth.

clue.text: Shakespearean character loves — right, left and centre

indicators.note: centre says the right, left and and pieces sit in the middle of the two loves

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so two loves are two O letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lover plays the field, with romances to right, left and centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right, left and centre' looks like the idiom for everywhere; R, L, AND go in the 'centre' of two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is the young hero of Shakespeare's As You Like It who loves Rosalind.

clue.text: Lupin's growth recorded in this?

parts.note: Lupin is not a plant but Lupin Pooter, son of the narrator in the Grossmiths' comic novel of 1892, whose doings are recorded in his father's journal

explanation.definitionFit: The Grossmith brothers' comic novel is Charles Pooter's journal, in which his son Lupin features.

clue.text: Diana leaves board for position in church

indicators.note: Diana leaves means her short form is taken out of the board word

parts.note: a directorate is a board of directors
Di is the short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: Princess Diana quits a company board for a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes DI out of DIRECTORATE, leaving RECTORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectorate is the office or tenure of a rector, a parish priest.

clue.text: Capital Henry invested in food store

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as if clothed in the food store

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
H is the SI symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry puts his capital into a delicatessen business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money invested, but it is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi (with New Delhi) is the seat of India's government, its capital city.

clue.text: Serious, reflecting the gravity of the situation

definitions.meaning: grave, weighty, as in a ... discussion

definitions.text: reflecting the gravity of the situation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weighty in tone and having physical weight under gravity.

clue.text: Intransigent type in ship, standing on stern

indicators.note: standing on says the ship word sits after the stern word in this across entry

parts.note: stern means hard, severe
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: An uncompromising sailor stands firm at the back of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like the back of the ship, but it is the adjective HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refuses to compromise on policy is an uncompromising extremist.

clue.text: Vessel finding a haven, initially, in no island

indicators.note: in says the short pieces go inside the no-plus-island pair

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of haven

explanation.surface: A ship finds a safe harbour where there is no island to shelter it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the short pieces between the other two; Sark is a small car-free Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ark built to survive the Flood is a famous boat.

clue.text: Support a system of lines used in this sort of school

parts.note: to second is to support a proposal
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a system of lines

explanation.surface: Someone backs a railway network serving a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'system of lines' suggests a ruled page, but it is the railway abbreviation RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school is the type children attend after primary, around ages 11 to 18.

clue.text: Altogether fascinated by odd bits of Troy

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on or fascinated by it

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first and third letters of Troy

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly absorbed by scattered remains of ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes letters 1 and 3 of TROY, giving TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means entirely or as a whole, a synonym of completely.

clue.text: Force I had put in before noon i.e. twelve o'clock

indicators.note: put in says the short pieces go inside the force word

parts.note: might means force or power

indicators.note: before says the I-had piece comes ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone forced into action before noon, at twelve o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before noon' suggests the morning, but it only orders the pieces that are 'put in' the force word.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight is twelve o'clock at night, the start of a new day.

clue.text: Measuring devices used in science

definitions.meaning: an optic is a device on an upside-down bottle in a British pub that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits
the branch of physics that studies light and vision

explanation.definitionFit: The plural names both pub spirit-measuring gadgets and the physics of light.

clue.text: Doctor splitting money raised by a lottery

indicators.note: splitting says the doctor letters go into the middle of the money word
raised in a down entry means the money word is read upwards

parts.note: loot is slang for money
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor divides the cash raised by a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the money word upwards to read TOOL, which the doctor's letters then split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum, a kind of prize draw.

clue.text: State carriage

definitions.meaning: an Australian state whose capital is Melbourne
a low, light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after the queen

explanation.surface: A ceremonial carriage used on state occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both an Australian state and a style of horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Note missed by clarinet ruined musical performance

indicators.note: ruined says the remaining letters are wrecked and rearranged
missed by means the note letter is left out of the instrument

parts.note: N is a note in the sense of the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A clarinettist misses a note and spoils the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed by' drops N from CLARINET, and 'ruined' rearranges CLARIET.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert given by a soloist or small group.

clue.text: Record unfinished church as subject to fire damage

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the record word is cut

parts.note: a score is a record of points in a game

explanation.surface: An unfinished church is recorded as fire-damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the E from SCORE, leaving SCOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface of something, singe.

clue.text: West Indian who's lower in the order than 1 ac?

definitions.meaning: a native of Dominica, a Caribbean island

definitions.text: who's lower in the order than 1 ac?
definitions.meaning: a friar or nun of the order founded by St Dominic ranks below the convent head of 1 across

explanation.surface: A Caribbean islander is ranked beneath someone else in a hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to 1 across, the head of a religious community; a member of St Dominic's order ranks below her.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person from Dominica and a member of the religious order of St Dominic.

clue.text: Parrot wife traded for ring in this city out East

indicators.note: traded for means the wife letter is swapped out for the ring letter

parts.note: a macaw is a large brightly coloured parrot
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a parrot and a wedding ring in a Far Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traded for' swaps the W of MACAW for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Macao (Macau) is a former Portuguese territory on the south coast of China, in the Far East.

clue.text: General supporting me in fight

indicators.note: supporting in a down entry puts the general below the me word

parts.note: taken as written
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A general backs me up in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece 'supporting' another sits beneath it; Lee is the American Civil War general.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand brawl, a scuffle.

clue.text: Foreign agreement on port wine

indicators.note: on in an across entry puts the agreement after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: An overseas deal is struck on port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' reads as one thing, but 'port' is RIO and 'wine' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of the same name.

clue.text: Second in command allowed to put on gear for opera

indicators.note: put on says the other pieces are placed after the gear in this across entry

parts.note: rig means equipment or gear

indicators.note: Second in picks the second letter of command

parts.note: let means allowed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deputy commander is permitted to don his kit before an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second in command' looks like a deputy, but it is the O in 'command'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigoletto is Verdi's opera about a hunchbacked court jester.

clue.text: Her lover's bookcase was sensational!

parts.note: read 'bookcase' as book case: the obscenity trial over D. H. Lawrence's novel about her lover caused a sensation in 1960

explanation.definitionFit: She is the title heroine of the novel whose 1960 obscenity trial was a famous court case.
